title: Message in a bottleneck: Nested founder effects from French Polynesia to Rapa Nui and Hawaiʻi
title_zh: 瓶颈中的信息：从法属波利尼西亚到拉帕努伊和夏威夷的嵌套创始效应
abstract: Founder effects can lead to strong, population-specific allele frequency differentiation, including autosomal recessive conditions. Their characterization in European-descent groups, such as the Finnish and Amish, has resulted in actionable genetic tests for each. We show that Polynesians experienced order-of-magnitude stronger cumulative founder effects during their settlement of Eastern Polynesia. Using whole-genome sequences spanning Polynesia, we show that two of the most bottlenecked populations are Hawaiʻi and Easter Island (Rapa Nui) and that these two most closely genetically related yet geographically distant islands were likely settled by the same ultravoyagers with earlier ancestral roots in Mangareva. We identify clinical genetic variation generated by this sequence of successive oceanic founder events, including a loss-of-function FAN1 mutation common in Eastern Polynesia (>1%) but entirely absent from gnomAD.
abstract_zh: 创始效应可导致强烈的、特定人群的等位基因频率差异，包括常染色体隐性疾病。在欧洲后裔群体（如芬兰人和阿米什人）中的表征已导致针对每个群体的可操作遗传检测。我们显示，波利尼西亚人在东波利尼西亚定居期间经历了比其他群体强一个数量级的累积创始效应。利用跨越波利尼西亚的全基因组测序数据，我们发现最受瓶颈影响的两个群体是夏威夷和复活节岛（拉帕努伊），这两个在基因上最相近但地理上相距甚远的岛屿，可能是由同一批超远航者定居的，这些航者的早期祖先根源于曼加雷瓦。我们识别出由这一系列连续海洋创始事件产生的临床遗传变异，包括一种在东波利尼西亚常见的失活FAN1突变（>1%），但在gnomAD中完全缺失。
